limitations: Small n: held-out researcher n=90 (47 MATCH, 43 NON_MATCH), work n=5 (5 MATCH, 0 NON_MATCH). One pair moves researcher recall by about 2.1 points and precision by about 2 points; no confidence intervals are computed.
Bounded subset: all pairs come from the DBLP 1K sample run (rootI, snapshot dblp-1k), not the full corpus; results do not transfer to the full DBLP file or other sources.
Single labeler: gold labels were written by one human; no inter-annotator agreement exists. Pcd31c083d4d9 (deterministic FP) may be a label disagreement rather than a policy error.

No citation features: citation-neighbourhood evidence does not exist in this corpus; venue and affiliation are not persisted by Phase 04, so venue_compat and affiliation_compat are absent in real runs.

Work has no held-out NON_MATCH (work: 5 MATCH, 0 NON_MATCH held-out; the only work NON_MATCH is in calibration). Work metrics are DESCRIPTIVE only; precision, specificity and FP are not measurable and no precision conclusion is drawn for work. Work recall 0.6 (3 of 5) rests on 5 pairs.

LLM path NOT EXECUTED: provider decision pending (Bedrock vs. Anthropic API, $25 budget). P2 was skipped by the human. No LLM call was made and no API key was read. The adjudication cache is absent. Unresolved pairs stay unresolved and are counted in the unresolved rate (researcher held-out 21 of 90, 0.2333); the llm path row is 0 for everything.

N1 DEFERRED: the 0.92 family_jw ORCID-name route admits Chen/Cheng-type pairs. Of the 12 held-out errors none comes from the N1 route (no error has orcid_agreement 1 and family_exact < 1: the researcher exact_id errors are ORCID disagreements, the other FPs/FNs are probabilistic or deterministic). Whether any held-out TP used the N1 route is not determined: stored predictions carry no features. Held-out exact_id researcher accepted had 0 FP.
N2 DEFERRED (not addressed in this evaluation; no change was made to policy, thresholds, features or split).

Calibration researcher accept=0.77 sits at a recall cliff: calibration recall is 0.9143 (TP 64, FN 6) at 0.77 and drops to 0.8286 (TP 58, FN 12) at 0.78. Three held-out researcher FNs have scores 0.733, 0.755 and 0.761, just under 0.77, consistent with that cliff. The two held-out probabilistic FPs sit at 0.779 and 0.808 (the third held-out FP, Pcd31c083d4d9, is deterministic).
Calibration numbers are in-sample (the thresholds were chosen on them) and are not held-out numbers. The sensitivity table below is a calibration-split table and was not used to evaluate held-out.

Rule-set design: the deterministic and exact-id rules (policy rules 0, 1b and the deterministic rule list) were designed after seeing candidate pairs only through the blind review queue and Phase 04 run output (blind queue: no score or predicted outcome). The rule set is not independent of the sampled pairs; the held-out pairs are drawn from the same queue.
Work threshold: calibration had 8 work rows (7 MATCH, 1 NON_MATCH); the work thresholds (accept=reject=0.79, empty LLM band) are almost unconstrained and are reported, not defended.
Held-out was evaluated once with the frozen policy; any further evaluation is a new disclosed evaluation requiring human authorization.

exact_id-path metrics are partly circular: the blind review queue shows ORCIDs and DOIs to the labeler, so labels on exact_id pairs may be influenced by the same identifiers the exact_id rules use (Part A review L6 required this disclosure).

Possible label inconsistencies were observed by the reviewer for the human to audit: the same two names (Lei Ren / Luquan Ren) are labelled both MATCH and NON_MATCH in different rows, and P254a0c96efc2 (same name, same paper) is labelled NON_MATCH. No label was edited. Any relabel invalidates the frozen calibration and requires a new, disclosed evaluation.
heldoutRowsRead: Evaluate scored all 95 held-out rows once.
